The changes to `unix_epoch_to_nstime` appear to avoid using the `%s` format specifier, which is *not* documented in the Single UNIX Specification as applying either to `strptime()` or `strftime()`, and thus *should* be avoided by us, especially if there are `strptime()` (or `strftime()`) implementations out there that don't implement it.

Furthermore, given that it's used to, according to the editcap man page, parse "Unix epoch timestamps (floating point format)", and given that it's converting those to seconds and nanoseconds since the Epoch, there's no need to involve `struct tm` at all - and doing so risks the local time offset being involved in the conversion.

So that change should probably be made separately and backported to earlier releases, and should take whatever is before the decimal point (if any) and directly stuff it into the seconds portion (if it fits) and take whatever comes after the decimal point and stuff it into the nanoseconds portion (if it fits).

commits_data.title: Build with NetBSD's strptime()
commits_data.message:
Build with NetBSD's strptime()

Replace our strptime code, which is from gnulib,
with the simpler and better NetBSD implementation.

This changes the ws_strptime() stub to unconditionally use
the internal implementation. Previously it would use the
system implementation of available. This is still possible
but is opt-in, i.e., code should add the necessary #ifdefs
and assume responsability for handling non-portable formats
or providing limited functionality on some platforms.

Text import allows the user to specify the strptime()
format freely, so in that case it makes sense to use the
system's implementation, and pass the responsability
for understanding the implementation and the supported
specifiers to the user.

Only fall back to our implementation if the system libc
lacks a strptime().
